root_cause: TerminalHistoryStore.Save writes the entire JSON file via os.WriteFile on every Save call (every command entered triggers Save via the UI). No write-coalescing or debounce; each Save produces a full file rewrite. Plain os.WriteFile is also non-atomic.
impact: Every command a user types triggers a full JSON serialize + write of up to maxHistorySize (500) entries. Hundreds of full-file rewrites per active day. Crash mid-write can corrupt the file (contradicting STORE-09 quarantine).
fix_sketch: Coalesce writes via a debounce timer (e.g. 500ms) and flush on shutdown; switch to atomicWriteFile for parity with ConnectionStore/SettingsStore; consider an append-only JSONL file.
verification: tail -f modification time of terminal-history.json while typing in a terminal tab.

root_cause: RecentStore.Record does not debounce — every Record call re-marshals the full id slice (up to maxRecent=20) and rewrites recent.json via plain os.WriteFile. Not using atomicWriteFile so a crash mid-write can lose the file.
impact: Per connection-open and per reconnect a fresh JSON marshal + non-atomic file write happens. Inconsistent with the rest of the store package which fixed STORE-09.
fix_sketch: Use atomicWriteFile; coalesce writes via a debounced background flusher; consider an append-only log.
verification: Open + close connections in quick succession; stat recent.json mtime after each.

root_cause: AISessionStore.Save / Load marshals / unmarshals the entire ai-sessions.json into memory on every save. AIMessageEntry retains Content verbatim plus an optional _rawApiMsg blob. No sliding-window or token-budget truncation.
impact: Long AI sessions with large tool results blow up the file and the Go-side decode cost grows linearly. The frontend also re-clones this blob across the Wails bridge. Together this contributes to the 400+ MB WebKit memory pressure on long sessions.
fix_sketch: Cap Messages per session (sliding window of last N turns or token-budgeted). Drop RawAPIMsg after it's been transcoded into the visible message. Stream-write the JSON via json.Encoder instead of json.MarshalIndent.
verification: Run a long Claude Code session; monitor ai-sessions.json size and RSS via pprof heap.

root_cause: SaveConnections (app.go:349) emits the full ConnectionStoreData (groups + every ConnectionConfig including long strings like K8sConfigInline) on every change. On a 100-connection list this is hundreds of KB marshalled across the bridge per write.
impact: Every connection edit triggers a full-state push to the frontend, which WebKit JS-clones. The frontend store retains the full list, dominating WebKit JS heap.
fix_sketch: Emit a delta (id + changed fields) instead of the full blob. Frontend should subscribe to a 'patch' channel; reserve full-state push for app boot only.
verification: Chrome DevTools: profile JSON.parse cost on the frontend while editing connections in dev mode.

root_cause: ConnectionStore.Save marshals the full ConnectionConfig slice (including PostLoginExpectSteps, K8sConfigInline YAML strings) with json.MarshalIndent even for a single-field edit.
impact: Each connection edit re-serializes the entire list (KeyPath / PostLoginScript / K8sConfigInline can be large). On a 100-connection user every UI edit triggers a multi-KB JSON encode + atomic rename + fsync.
fix_sketch: Use json.NewEncoder without indent (drop MarshalIndent in production). Consider a flat-file-per-connection layout, or at minimum diff-and-write only the changed connection.
verification: go test -bench=BenchmarkConnectionStoreSave ./backend/store/...; pprof cpu for SaveConnections under repeated single-row edits.

root_cause: CommandsStore.List does a full directory scan + reads every commands/*.md file via readCapped on every call. No in-memory cache; on each call it also reads commands.json and frequently rewrites it (the default-fill loop sets changed = true the first time a missing-pref is encountered).
impact: Each call does O(N) directory reads + O(N) file reads + full prefs.json read + (often) full prefs.json write. On a commands-rich workspace this is hundreds of syscalls and full file rewrites per UI open.
fix_sketch: Cache the merged List result and invalidate only on fsnotify events (or on savePaths). Skip the pref-default-fill write during read; defer the migration to a one-time startup pass.
verification: strace -e trace=openat,read,write,fsync uniterm; observe repeated read+write on UI open.

root_cause: SkillsStore.List reads every skill's SKILL.md (and probes references/ + scripts/ via dirHasFiles and countFiles, each of which opens a directory) on every invocation. No caching.
impact: Every skills panel render or agent prompt injection triggers O(skills) file opens + a full prefs.json read + frequently a full prefs.json rewrite. With 50 skills that's 150 syscalls per List call.
fix_sketch: Cache the merged list keyed by skills-dir mtime; use a single os.ReadDir per skill dir and partition files/subdirs in-memory instead of three separate dir reads.
verification: strace -c -e trace=openat uniterm; compare syscall count on skills panel open vs a cached variant.

root_cause: SettingsStore.Save marshals the entire AppSettings with json.MarshalIndent and atomic-writes, including CustomTerminalThemes (full TerminalThemeColors for each) and the Keyboard map. MarshalIndent allocates a buffer the size of the output for whitespace alone.
impact: Every settings UI tick (theme select, font size bump, custom theme add) rewrites the whole settings.json. On modest SSDs the fsync blocks the UI thread for a few ms each time.
fix_sketch: Persist only the changed subtree (split into multiple files: theme.json, terminal.json, ai.json, keybindings.json) OR write a JSON patch. Coalesce successive saves (debounce 250ms). Drop MarshalIndent in production.
verification: Drag the font-size slider back and forth; observe settings.json rewrite count vs UI event count.

root_cause: SettingsStore.Load takes the write lock for the entire duration of disk I/O + keychain backfill + default-fill. Any concurrent Save blocks behind it; the read returns only after the file is fully decoded.
impact: First load on a cold start blocks all other Save calls (and keychain I/O). On macOS the keychain call is synchronous via the Security framework — a slow keychain response stalls UI load.
fix_sketch: Use sync.RWMutex for reads, hold the write lock only during the keychain backfill + needsSave rewrite. Cache the parsed AppSettings in memory so subsequent Loads return instantly.
verification: pprof block profile on cold start; observe the settings lock hold time.

root_cause: ConnectionStore.populatePasswords re-iterates every connection, calls the keychain once per password, and if any plaintext passwords existed, takes the write lock and does an atomic write of the full file under that lock.
impact: Every Load() on a connection list with N passwords makes N blocking keychain calls (synchronous Security framework on macOS). With 50 passwords that's 50 syscalls before the UI can render. Worst case: many tabs edit connections, migration rewrites the full file under a write lock that other tabs are waiting on.
fix_sketch: Backfill passwords asynchronously after returning Load() (mark conns as PasswordPending so the UI can prompt). Coalesce the migration rewrite to a single startup-only pass.
verification: pprof CPU + block on cold start with 100 connections; observe keychain stalls.

root_cause: CommandsStore.CreateCommand / SaveCommand call os.WriteFile on the .md file directly (no atomic rename, no fsync) while also rewriting commands.json. A crash between the two writes leaves the .md updated but commands.json stale (or vice versa).
impact: Two non-atomic writes per Create / Save / Delete, with a window where user-visible state is inconsistent. On power loss the .md can exist without a pref entry, or a pref can reference a deleted file.
fix_sketch: Use atomicWriteFile (the helper the rest of the package uses) for both writes. Order: write prefs first, then the .md, so an orphan pref (no .md) is recoverable on next List.
verification: kill -9 the process between the two writes; observe inconsistency.

root_cause: copyDir uses filepath.Walk that calls os.Lstat + os.Open + os.Create per file with no batching. copyFileWithoutSymlinks opens a fresh file handle for each file and uses io.Copy with default 32KB buffer; for many small reference files this is overhead-bound.
impact: Skill imports with many small reference files pay per-file syscall overhead. io.Copy uses a default 32KB buffer that is wasteful for tiny files. No bufio.Reader or sync.Pool reuse.
fix_sketch: Use io.CopyBuffer with a pooled []byte (sync.Pool) and reuse open handles when iterating. Skip files with identical content (mtime/size check).
verification: go test -bench=BenchmarkCopyDir ./backend/store/...; measure for a 50-file skill.

root_cause: queryStrings and queryAny allocate a fresh map[string]any per row plus a fresh []any value holder per row. For a 10k-row x 20-col result that's 10k maps + 200k interface{} slots.
impact: Big DB scans (10k-row table dumps) blow up Go heap and bridge-clone cost when the result is sent to the frontend. Combined with no streaming of QueryResult over the bridge the Wails call blocks for tens of MB of JSON encode.
fix_sketch: Stream results back to the frontend via a Wails event or via paged callbacks. Provide a row-count cap. Use []map[string]any only for small results; for large results return rows + columns separately and stream.
verification: Open a table with 10k rows in the data viewer; observe pprof heap inuse and p99 latency.

root_cause: scanToString calls fmt.Sprintf("%v", v) for any non-[]byte value. fmt.Sprintf allocates a fmt.buffer + parses the format string per call.
impact: Every non-string column (int, float, time.Time, nil) in every row hits fmt.Sprintf. For a 10k-row scan that's 200k Sprintf calls.
fix_sketch: Switch on common types (string, int64, float64, time.Time, bool) and use type assertions / strconv.Format* directly. Fall back to fmt only as a last resort.

root_cause: Postgres GetTableSchema issues three serial round-trips (columns, primary keys, indexes) per call. For a database-tree UI panel that walks every table this is 3*N queries. MySQL/SQLServer have the same shape.
impact: Open a 200-table database in the schema browser - 600 round-trips to the server. On a remote DB with 50ms RTT that's 30s of UI load.
fix_sketch: Cache the schema for the lifetime of the connection; serve subsequent GetTableSchema calls from cache; invalidate only on user-driven schema mutation. Same cache applies to all providers.
verification: Time the schema browser open for a 200-table DB over a 50ms RTT link.

root_cause: mysqlProvider DSN sets timeout=10s but no ConnMaxLifetime / ConnMaxIdleTime / MaxOpenConns / MaxIdleConns. database/sql defaults to unlimited open conns and unbounded lifetime - a long-lived tab can accumulate idle TCP sockets to the DB, and a server-side timeout (wait_timeout) eventually drops them.
impact: Stale connections cause 'invalid connection' or 'bad connection' errors after MySQL's wait_timeout (default 28800s) elapses. No pooling cap means a busy DB tab can open hundreds of idle sockets over a long session.
fix_sketch: In NewDB after sql.Open call db.SetMaxOpenConns(10), db.SetMaxIdleConns(5), db.SetConnMaxLifetime(5*time.Minute), db.SetConnMaxIdleTime(2*time.Minute). Same for postgresProvider / oracleProvider / sqlserverProvider.
verification: Inspect netstat for the uniterm process during a long-running DB session; observe open socket count growth.
